a + (—a) = 0.
proof Suppose x is in a and y is in —a. Then —y is not in a, so — y > x. Hence
x + y < 0, so x + y is in 0. Thus every member of a + (—a) is in 0.
It is a little more difficult to go in the other direction. If z is in 0, then —z > 0.
According to the lemma, there is some x in a, and some y not in a, with y not the
smallest element of Q — a, such that y — x = — z. This equation can be written
x + (—y) = z. Since x is in a, and —y is in —a, this proves that z is in a + (—or). |
